item.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Is the Greatest Line in Sci-Fi History
item.description: Certain lines of dialogue become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context. The words have long since transcended their original context.

item.title: 5 Most Perfect 1980s Games That Nobody Remembers
item.description: The 1980s wasn't the decade video games were born; the origins of the medium go back a further 20 years, through the likes of Spacewar! and Pong . But it was in the 1980s that video games grew up, exploding in popularity and complexity and establishing many of their defining stars. It was the decade that gave us Mario and Zelda, Pac-Man, Final Fantasy, Prince of Persia, and SimCity. But it also gave us some much more obscure titles that have since fallen by the wayside. Here are five fantastic '80s games that might have been forgotten, but still have something to teach us.

item.title: Every Legend of Zelda Movie Character and Cast Member Confirmed So Far
item.description: Nintendo is attempting something it hasn't done in more than 30 years : make a live-action adaptation of its video games. The Legend of Zelda from Sony Pictures and Nintendo is slated for release in April 2027, bringing the fantasy role-playing game franchise to life in a way never seen before. (Well, except for that one Japanese commercial for The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past with a rappin' Link.)

item.title: 10 Near-Perfect Netflix Sci-Fi Shows That Hook You in the First Scene
item.description: Not every great sci-fi show needs to start with a bang, but the best ones know how to grab your attention from the very first frame. Whether it’s a gruesome public execution in the middle of a cultural revolution, a child stepping into a smoke-filled battleground littered with corpses, or an alien organism mutating a host in seconds, the most compelling series understand the power of a great first impression. Such shows offer something tangible enough to keep you glued to your seat before the opening credits even roll.
